name: Zero (Rocicorp)
tagline: Query-driven sync engine: clients run ZQL locally against a Postgres-backed cache for instant UIs.
description: Zero is a sync engine from Rocicorp, the makers of Replicache. A zero-cache server replicates your PostgreSQL database into SQLite and keeps client-side caches up to date. Clients write ZQL queries (relational, with nested relationships) that answer instantly from local data and are kept live by incremental view maintenance on the server. Writes are custom mutators that run optimistically on the client and authoritatively in a Postgres transaction on your server. Zero reached 1.0 and is under very active development. It is aimed at snappy web apps like Linear-style tools rather than offline-for-days mobile apps.

pricing.notes: Free and open source; you run zero-cache yourself.

scale.notes: zero-cache supports multiple view-syncer nodes; write capacity is that of the upstream Postgres.

strengths: Relational queries with nested relationships answered from local cache
Incremental view maintenance keeps many live queries cheap
Uses your existing Postgres as the source of truth
Custom mutators keep server-side validation in normal code
weaknesses: Not designed for long offline write sessions
You operate zero-cache yourself; no first-party managed service
TypeScript/web focus; native mobile SDKs are limited
useCases: Highly interactive SaaS web apps (issue trackers, editors, dashboards)
Adding instant UI updates over an existing Postgres schema
